Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together a compact acceptance checklist (attached) and a short summary below so your finops/legal have concrete items to sign off against. High level: we propose an acceptance window to lock economics 7 business days before contract signature, with a fallback policy baked into the MAP if traffic or cache hit-rate assumptions miss by >15%.

Key acceptance items (summary):
- Tokens/$ target: baseline model (redwood-v1-standard) priced at 0.0009 $/token inference unit; target production effective rate must be <= 0.00095 $/token after batching + KV caching for the first 60 days.
- Caching assumptions: expected prefix/KV cache hit-rate 55% (median) for mapped prompt families; MAP acceptance threshold if observed hit-rate >= 40% in evaluation sims. Fallback: if hit-rate < 40%, automatic downgrade to pre-agreed lower-cost model variant (redwood-v1-lite) with explicit quality guardrail.
- Batching assumptions: average request concurrency projected 180 qps across peak shards; we assume dynamic batching with 16–32 sequence aggregation and 25ms additional queuing latency; verification requires running our eval harness for 4 consecutive 4‑hour windows that mirror customer traffic profile.
- Financial gating: if observed unit cost > 5% above target after evaluation, require an executive sign-off and apply a 30-day remediation plan (tuning batching, quantization profile) before final tiered pricing is applied.

I've attached the MAP_cost_acceptance_checklist.xlsx and a token snapshot PDF. Markus and Laura — tagging you for technical confirmation and timeline commitment. Proposed close timeline: lock economics by 2026-05-16 to enable legal review and DocuSign the week of 2026-05-24.

Next steps I propose:
1) Mark internal owners and run the eval sim (Markus) — due 2026-05-12.
2) Share sim results with Olive finops/legal and convene 30-min readout (Diego/Laura) — target 2026-05-13.
3) Apply fallback clauses in SOW and circulate redlines to legal — target 2026-05-14.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the checklist.

Thanks,

Adding a few technical clarifications from the solutions side so the acceptance checklist is actionable:

- Batching: the 16–32 aggregation window is measured by token count and arrival window; for OLIVE traffic profile we should target adaptive batching with a 50ms max wait cap to avoid tail latency violations. I'll include raw sim config in the Drive folder.
- Caching: prefix cache hit-rate is workload dependent. For short-form prompt families (templates + few-shot context) we see 60–70% hit-rates in our internal sims; but with high variability. The 40% threshold Diego proposed is conservative and buyable.
- Quantization & fallback: if we trigger the fallback to a quantized variant, we must run a small QA eval (1000 prompt pairs) to verify no regression >2% on the quality metric the customer cares about (ROUGE/F1 or custom rubric). We'll instrument that as part of the eval plan.

I'll own the sims and the preflight config. ETA: sim artifacts uploaded by EOD 2026-05-11; results posted to Drive 2026-05-12 morning.

-Markus
